title: Security testing coordination: roles, log format, and remediation matrix
content:
Purpose and audience:

This doc is an operational coordination and source-of-truth for upcoming external security testing engagements (red team and third-party pen tests) that intersect RBAC v2, audit-log collection, SIEM export, and evidence automation. Audience: SecOps, Platform SRE, Serving Runtime owners, Product Security, and the external testing vendor.

High-level objectives:
- Define owner-level responsibilities during active engagement (who collects what, who reviews findings).
- Provide the exact audit-log export format and SIEM field mappings the vendor should use for evidence ingestion.
- Describe automated evidence collection hooks and scripts to be enabled during the test window.
- Publish a remediation matrix template mapping finding types to owners, severity, and expected SLA.

Engagement assumptions and constraints:
- The vendor will run tests in a staging environment that mirrors production networking and auth flows. No direct production writes unless explicitly approved in a scoped escalation (see JIRA-SEC-3421).
- Sources of truth for logs: internal API gateway logs, identity service (OIDC) audit trail, RBAC decision logs, and GPU-node system logs.
- SIEM destination: our Elastic cluster (index: redwood-security-logs-YYYY.MM). If vendor prefers file dumps, use NDJSON with the schema below.

Coordination and roles (primary contact list):
- Engagement lead (vendor liaison): Ethan Brooks — coordinates test schedule, scope updates, and report delivery.
- Evidence ingestion and SIEM owner: Maya Chen — responsible for running the ingestion job and validating mapping.
- RBAC / Auth SME: Luis Ortega — validates policy test vectors, interprets decision logs.
- Incident contact and escalation: Priya Natarajan — final authority for halting tests and approving active mitigations.
- Serving runtime SME: Samir Nair — assists with kernel-level or runtime-specific findings.

Pre-test checklist (two weeks out):
- Confirm scope in JIRA-SEC-3421 and get signed approval from Product Security and Legal.
- Create an ephemeral ingestion index in Elastic and grant vendor read-only access for validation.
- Enable verbose audit logging for RBAC v2 test users; TTL set to 90 days for the test window.
- Deploy evidence collection container (see linked repo PR #678) with collector mode set to "pen-test".
- Smoke test a sample scenario (auth->token->inference->cache invalidation) and confirm log flow end-to-end.

Audit-log export format (required) — NDJSON line per event (fields MUST be present):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC string
- event_id: UUID
- source: one of [api-gateway, identity, rbac-decision, serving-runtime, gpu-node]
- event_type: short string (auth.attempt, auth.grant, rbac.check, model.invoke, cache.evict, syscall.exec)
- user_id: internal user id or service principal (if unauthenticated, set to "anonymous")
- client_ip: IPv4/6 string
- resource: the resource path (e.g., /v1/models/gpt4-infer)
- action: high-level action verb (read, write, execute, assume-role, token-refresh)
- decision: allow | deny | partial (for partial grants)
- reason: free-text reason or policy id (e.g., "policy:team-read-only")
- request_id: correlation id from gateway if present
- raw_payload_hash: sha256 of the request payload when applicable
- metadata: stringified JSON with small diagnostic keys (env, region, node_id)

Note: 'metadata' must be a JSON string (no nested structures in the NDJSON top-level); the ingestion pipeline will parse it into nested fields inside Elastic.

Minimum retention and privacy considerations:
- For pen-test evidence, retain logs for 90 days in the ephemeral index. Production retention still follows compliance policy (365 days for security indexes).
- Redact PII before sharing externally. Any request payloads containing PII must be hashed into raw_payload_hash and recorded as "PII_REDACTED" in the 'metadata' field.

Evidence automation steps to enable (scripts and hooks):
1) Collector container (repo: infra/log-collector) — run in collector mode 'pen-test' which sets higher sampling and attaches request_id correlation headers to all generated requests.
2) RBAC wrapper instrumentation — a small middleware that logs rbac.check events with policy snapshots. Toggle via env RBAC_INSTRUMENT=true.
3) Gateway export job — run the nightly exporter with --index-prefix=redwood-pt-evidence and set --shards=1 to avoid hot shards during ingestion.
4) SIEM ingestion verification — Maya will run the verify_ingest.sh which checks 100 random events for schema conformance and presence of correlation ids.

Example NDJSON event (single line):
{"timestamp":"2025-02-19T18:12:07Z","event_id":"2a9f5c12-4b7e-4f3a-9cde-0a1b2c3d4e5f","source":"api-gateway","event_type":"model.invoke","user_id":"svc-account-data-ingest","client_ip":"10.1.4.12","resource":"/v1/models/llama-3/infer","action":"execute","decision":"allow","reason":"policy:default-execute","request_id":"req-57a3b","raw_payload_hash":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...","metadata":"{"env":"staging","region":"us-east-1","node_id":"gpu-12"}"}

SIEM queries and example investigation steps (Elastic/KQL and example SPL):
- Find all denied RBAC checks for a user in the last 24h:
  KQL: source:rbac-decision AND event_type:rbac.check AND decision:deny AND user_id:"<user>" AND timestamp:[now-24h TO now]
- Track a request through the system by request_id:
  KQL: request_id:"req-57a3b" OR correlation_id:"req-57a3b"
- Example SPL (for Splunk users): index=redwood-security source=rbac-decision decision=deny user_id=<user> | stats count by reason

Findings triage and remediation matrix (template):
Columns: finding_id | summary | source | severity | initial_owner | recommended_fix | quick_mitigations | target_date | status | jira_ticket
- Severity levels: critical (RCE, auth bypass), high (priv escalation, data exfil), medium (info leak), low (misconfig).
- Example row: FND-2025-007 | token replay on internal gateway | api-gateway | high | Platform SRE | enforce anti-replay nonce + token binding | rotate test tokens, add WAF rule | 2025-02-28 | open | JIRA-SEC-3490

Remediation SLAs (for pen-test findings):
- Critical: acknowledge within 2 business hours, remediation plan in 24 hours, fix or compensating control within 3 business days unless blocker documented.
- High: acknowledge within 1 business day, mitigation or patch plan within 5 business days.
- Medium: acknowledge within 3 business days, patch in 30 days.
- Low: acknowledge within 7 business days, patch in next quarterly schedule.

Reporting cadence and artifacts:
- Daily standup during active engagement (15m) — attendance: Engagement lead, Evidence owner, RBAC SME, SRE on-call.
- End-of-day evidence bundle (NDJSON + index snapshot + verify_ingest.log) delivered to vendor and stored at s3://redwood-pen-test-evidence/{engagement-id}/dates
- Final report: vendor provides a narrative + prioritized findings. Redwood will add remediation matrix entries and produce a joint remediation sign-off doc.

Post-engagement tasks:
- Revert any verbose logging toggles and set TTLs back to default.
- Run log sampling job to ensure no PII leaked to the ephemeral index.
- Run regression tests for RBAC v2 policies and produce a small eval harness (see linked repo PR #678).
- Postmortem and lessons learned doc due 7 days after final report.

Open questions and decisions required (for Product Security):
- Do we permit live production write-Attempts for scoped RCE proof-of-concept? (decision pending in JIRA-SEC-3421)
- Confirm retention for vendor-supplied artifacts beyond 90 days. Legal and Privacy to advise.

Appendix A — Quick troubleshooting checklist if evidence fails to appear in Elastic:
- Confirm collector container is running and mode==pen-test.
- Check that request_id headers are being emitted by gateway (trace a sample request).
- Verify the exporter service account has write permissions to the ephemeral index.
- Validate NDJSON lines for trailing commas or broken JSON (common when long payloads are included).

Appendix B — Helpful links and references:
- infra/log-collector repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/678
- Active scope ticket: JIRA-SEC-3421
- Log schema spec draft: CONFLUENCE-SEC-LOG-SCHEMA-1234
- Slack channel for real-time coordination: #secops-thread-pen-test-2025

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally pragmatic — the goal is to be explicit about which logs we expect and where they should land. We will iterate on the schema once we get a vendor sample dump.
- Expect follow-ups from Platform SRE on shard/retention settings; those knobs may change during the test window to avoid impacting other workloads.

Unresolved items (tracked separately):
- Decide exact PII redaction fields (PII policy owner: legal).
- Confirm if GPU-node syscall logs must be retained beyond 90 days for forensic reasons.
